units: EER in percent; lower is better; deltas are B - A in EER points

protocols.codabench_dev: Official CodaBench dev (progress) phase: English + Bangla (unheard) cells, mean of 4 cells.
protocols.codabench_eval: Official CodaBench evaluation phase 1: English (heard) + Bangla (unheard), mean of 4 cells.
protocols.local_5fold: Local identity-disjoint 5-fold cross-validation on the 70 official (English) training identities; fixed trial files; 3 seeds x 5 folds x 90 epochs unless 'seeds' says otherwise; paired identity-level bootstrap.
protocols.local_5fold_terms: As local_5fold, scores include the fixed age/gender terms; term weights chosen on the same folds (small in-sample optimism).
protocols.urdu_holdout: Unseen-language proxy: 1/5 of MAV-Celeb v1 people held out per fold, no Urdu in training; per-seed scoring (phase2/language_transfer_fusion.py).
protocols.urdu_holdout_seedavg: Same Urdu holdout, but scores averaged over the 3 seeds before EER (local_validation/evaluate_language_transfer.py); not directly comparable with urdu_holdout.
protocols.german_holdout: Unseen-language confirmation: 1/5 of MAV-Celeb v3 people held out per fold, no German in training; per-seed scoring; never used for model selection.
protocols.unimodal_diagnostic: Voice-only or face-only verification/retrieval on unseen people (deterministic trials; Phase II).
protocols.simulation: Hidden-association simulation (GAMP-VF): labels of 77 external training people hidden; association recovery measured against the hidden truth.

experiments.title: V2 on the CodaBench dev (progress) leaderboard
experiments.question: How does the improved V2 system score officially?
experiments.interpretation: V2 is 7.8 points better than the official baseline on the dev leaderboard.

experiments.title: Evaluation-phase submissions #1-#3
experiments.question: Official scores of the submitted systems
experiments.interpretation: Local predictions transferred closely (eval #3: local -1.34, CodaBench -1.33). The system remains well behind the leaderboard median (22.47 on 13 Nov). Eval #4-#6 candidates have no submission record; the final challenge ranking is not available.

experiments.title: V1 -> V2: all-layer WavLM, SupCon, regularised heads
experiments.question: Do broader WavLM features and a supervised contrastive objective beat the V1 x-vector/ArcFace design?
experiments.hypothesis: Speaker-verification x-vectors discard traits shared with faces; all-layer WavLM keeps them.
experiments.interpretation: Both tracks improve significantly; V2 became the base system.

sources.extract: V1/V2 five-fold numbers and paired CI

experiments.title: V2 reference (3 seeds x 5 folds, epoch 90)
experiments.question: Reference numbers for every later paired comparison
experiments.interpretation: All Stage 3-4 comparisons are paired against these runs (runs/voice_aug/base).

experiments.title: Acoustic augmentation (50% clean)
experiments.question: Does 'Voice augmentation (clean 50%)' improve on V2?
experiments.hypothesis: Noise/reverb/codec augmentation regularises the voice branch.
experiments.interpretation: Worse on both tracks; augmented views move features far from their clip.

experiments.title: Acoustic augmentation (25% clean)
experiments.question: Does 'Voice augmentation (clean 25%)' improve on V2?
experiments.interpretation: Significantly worse (mean CI excludes 0).

experiments.title: Hyperbolic (Poincare) embeddings, tau = 0.1
experiments.question: Does 'Hyperbolic, tau 0.1' improve on V2?
experiments.hypothesis: A hierarchical geometry separates same-gender people better.
experiments.interpretation: Standard track -1.0 (significant), gender track unchanged; overlapped with the age/gender terms, so not carried forward.

experiments.title: Hyperbolic (Poincare) embeddings, tau = 0.2
experiments.question: Does 'Hyperbolic, tau 0.2' improve on V2?
experiments.interpretation: Standard -1.3 (significant), gender +0.25.

experiments.title: WavLM learned layer weights
experiments.question: Does 'Learned layer mix' improve on V2?
experiments.hypothesis: Learned layer weights beat the plain all-layer mean.
experiments.interpretation: No change; learned weights mildly prefer lower layers.

experiments.title: WavLM layer mix with temporal spread
experiments.question: Does 'Layer mix + temporal std' improve on V2?
experiments.hypothesis: Adding each layer's temporal spread adds speaker cues.
experiments.interpretation: Gender worse (CI excludes 0).

experiments.title: Per-clip WavLM layer attention
experiments.question: Does 'Per-clip layer attention' improve on V2?
experiments.hypothesis: Per-clip attention over layers selects useful layers.
experiments.interpretation: Significantly worse on both tracks (overfits with 70 identities).

experiments.title: ECAPA-TDNN instead of WavLM (70 identities)
experiments.question: Does 'ECAPA only (70 ids)' improve on V2?
experiments.hypothesis: A dedicated speaker-verification embedding carries finer person-specific cues.
experiments.interpretation: +3.2 mean: speaker embeddings alone lose the traits that link voice to face.

experiments.title: WavLM + ECAPA concatenation (70 identities)
experiments.question: Does 'WavLM + ECAPA (70 ids)' improve on V2?
experiments.interpretation: No gain with 70 identities (seed-1 gain vanished with seeds 2-3). Revisited in Phase II with 301 identities.

experiments.title: Bias-corrected age/gender consistency terms (V2)
experiments.question: Do fixed age/gender-consistency score terms help?
experiments.hypothesis: V2 under-uses age: impostors 20+ years apart are still accepted 20% of the time.
experiments.interpretation: Significant -0.8 mean, almost all on the standard track; submitted as eval #2 (CodaBench -1.1).

experiments.title: Learning curve over training identities
experiments.question: How much does EER fall with more training identities?
experiments.interpretation: About -1.6 EER points per doubling of identities on both tracks; motivated the external-data stage.

experiments.title: Alternative face backbones (V2 era)
experiments.question: Do sharper face features help?
experiments.interpretation: FaRL variants and FaRL + DINOv2 matched FaRL within noise; DINOv2 alone was worse. No per-variant numbers were logged.

experiments.title: Same-gender SupCon, hard negatives, prototype loss, OPL, GADH (V2 era)
experiments.question: Do alternative objectives help the gender track?
experiments.interpretation: No gains (same-gender SupCon: +1 point on standard). No per-variant numbers were logged.

experiments.title: Learned pairwise verifier
experiments.question: Does a learned matching head beat cosine?
experiments.interpretation: Training identities are almost perfectly separated, so the head learns an easy problem unlike unseen people. Numbers are from an earlier, different local setup and are not comparable with the 3-seed tables.

experiments.title: Pseudo-label recovery on 77 hidden identities
experiments.question: Can clustering + matching recover hidden face-voice associations reliably enough to train on?
experiments.hypothesis: Speaker clusters + cross-modal matching yield high-precision pseudo-pairs.
experiments.interpretation: Even with perfect grouping only 24% top-1 / 34% Hungarian; the 10% most confident matches are 57% correct. No mode reached usable precision.

experiments.title: Headroom: true labels of the 77 hidden people
experiments.question: Would perfect pseudo-labels help?
experiments.interpretation: No measurable gain (seed 1), so the simulation cannot show a pseudo-label benefit.

experiments.title: Voice-only speaker verification (same-gender impostors)
experiments.question: Is the voice input speaker-discriminative across sessions and languages?
experiments.interpretation: B0's voice input is session-dominated (30% EER across videos); ECAPA is ~3x better and nearly language-independent.

experiments.title: Face-only identity verification
experiments.question: Is the face input identity-discriminative?
experiments.interpretation: ArcFace ~1.8% vs FaRL 12.3% same-gender EER; FaRL tracks age/appearance strongly.
